holidays.name: National Escargot Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate snails on a plate: garlic butter, parsley, and a tiny fork. Adventurous eaters are encouraged to try the French delicacy, and everyone else is invited to admire it from a safe distance.
holidays.origin: National Escargot Day is an unofficial food observance popularized by food-holiday calendars. Escargot has been eaten in Europe since ancient times, and the dish became a signature of French cuisine.
holidays.funFact: The snails used for escargot are usually a species such as Helix pomatia, the Burgundy snail, and some French restaurants go through enormous quantities of them every year.

holidays.name: National Brother's Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate brothers, whether they are the ones who shared your childhood bedroom, stole your snacks, or became your lifelong best friend. Calling or texting him is encouraged, even if it's just a meme.
holidays.origin: Brother's Day is an unofficial observance with several competing dates around the world. May 24 is the date commonly cited in the United States, started by grassroots and card-company-style celebrations rather than any government.
holidays.funFact: Brother's Day has no single official date, so brothers in different countries can legitimately claim multiple days of appreciation per year.

holidays.name: Scavenger Hunt Day
holidays.description: A day for hunting down random objects, solving clues, and racing friends around town to find a rubber duck, a red button, and a menu from a restaurant. Teams compete for glory, bragging rights, and sometimes a trophy made of questionable craft supplies.
holidays.origin: Scavenger Hunt Day is an unofficial observance associated with the popular party game. Scavenger hunts became fashionable in the 1930s, when socialites such as Elsa Maxwell popularized them as high society party games.
holidays.funFact: In the 1930s, scavenger hunts became so popular that some of them reportedly included wild or absurd items on the list, such as a live animal or a famous person's signature.

holidays.name: Tiara Day
holidays.description: A day for wearing a sparkly tiara for no reason at all. Whether you're at your desk, walking the dog, or buying groceries, the point is to feel like royalty and make everyone else smile.
holidays.origin: Tiara Day is a playful, informal observance that grew from the dress-up and party culture, encouraging people to wear a crown simply for fun.
holidays.funFact: The word tiara comes from a Greek word for a type of Persian headdress, and for centuries it was worn by rulers as a symbol of power rather than as party attire.

holidays.name: Aegean Migration Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate the birds, butterflies, and other travelers that migrate across the Aegean region. It's a good excuse to look up at the sky and think about the long journeys that animals make every year.
holidays.origin: Awareness days related to migratory species are often organized by conservation groups. This one is part of the wider tradition of marking seasonal migrations with bird watching and nature walks.
holidays.funFact: Some migratory birds can fly for days without landing, and a few can even sleep while flying by resting half of their brain at a time.
